issues.problem: False-positive regression in dd40805: honest, everyday comparison and product-doc claims now fail the strict gate. Clause polarity is decided for the whole quote clause, and 'and' now splits a clause only before an auxiliary or an -ed word. So when a quote states the claim and then negates something else in the same sentence with a present-tense verb or an ellipsis ('Okta supports SCIM and OneLogin does not', 'supports SSO and lacks SCIM', 'runs on AWS and requires no agents', 'encrypts data at rest and never stores keys in plaintext', 'returns JSON and accepts no XML payloads'), the whole clause counts as negated and contradicts the honest claim. These passed at 3c517f0. The same root cause, already present before, also rejects 'with no X' ('supports SSO with no extra configuration', 'migrated ... in 2023 with no downtime', 'free tier with no time limit'), 'X, not Y' ('supports SAML, not LDAP') and comma-joined clauses ('integrates with Jira, and no plugin is required'). None of these is a documented limit: the documented negation limit is a fabrication passing ('a negated lowercase conjunct'), not honest claims failing. The same round also regressed one fabrication: NOT_ONLY_RE now strips 'not even', so 'Not even Acme supports SSO for enterprise customers' supports 'Acme supports SSO for enterprise customers' (caught at 3c517f0). Competitive comparisons ('A supports X and B does not') are exactly what this skill's solution-landscape runs quote, and FIX-BRIEF says a false positive is a bug.
issues.evidence: End to end through the SKILL.md gate (bin/e2e.sh, verify --dir --report --strict), REVF-H8a4-probe/runs/hon7.tsv, 8 honest pairs: HEAD dd40805 status fail, factual_not_supported 8, exit=1 (all 'partial', 'negation mismatch' except the range in issue 2); same TSV at 3c517f0: the first four ('Acme supports SAML single sign-on for enterprise customers' / '... and lacks SCIM provisioning'; '... on every plan' / '... and Initech does not'; 'Acme Cloud runs on AWS in three regions' / '... and requires no agents'; 'Acme encrypts customer data at rest with AES-256' / '... and never stores keys in plaintext') are 'supported'. bin/honest_neg4.py (18 honest product-doc pairs): HEAD rejects 11/18, 3c517f0 rejects 5/18. bin/score4.py: 7 honest mixed-polarity coordinations 'partial [negation mismatch]' at HEAD, supported at 3c517f0; 'with no extra configuration', 'with no setup fee', 'with no downtime', 'X, not Y' partial at both. REVF-H8a4-probe/runs/fab6.tsv line 7 ('Acme supports SSO for enterprise customers' vs 'Not even Acme supports SSO for enterprise customers'): HEAD 'supported', 3c517f0 'partial'. Sandbox mutation: making the AND_PREDICATE split unconditional keeps all 120 claim tests green, and no honest corpus pair has these shapes.
issues.suggested_fix: Scope the negation instead of flagging the whole clause: a negation cue negates the terms that follow it up to the next clause boundary, and an elliptical 'X does not' / 'X doesn't' at the end of a conjunct negates only the conjunct's own subject X (so 'A supports SSO and B does not' contradicts 'B supports SSO' but not 'A supports SSO'). Check alignment against the negated span, not the whole clause. Treat 'with no X' and 'no X' after a positive predicate as terms (like 'without X' and 'zero X'), split ', not Y' into its own negated span, and keep 'not even' a negation when it opens the clause (strip it only after another cue). Add these pairs verbatim to the honest corpus and the 'Not even' pair to the fabrications.

issues.problem: Figure, currency and year handling still lets fabrications through the strict gate, outside the documented limit classes (which name role swaps, antonyms/synonyms outside the tables, a negated lowercase conjunct and idioms), and contrary to quality-gates.md, which says every figure matches 'the same value, unit and currency' in a segment that shares a word, 'so swapped years or percentages fail'. (a) New in dd40805: number-word normalisation adds every number word joined by 'and', so 'between two and five days' becomes 'between 7 days' and 'four and five regions' becomes '9'. A fabricated '7 days' / '9 regions' is now supported (it was caught at 3c517f0), and the honest 'between 2 and 5 days' against 'between two and five days' fails. (b) Only $, EUR and GBP are currencies. Yen/yuan (¥, 'yen', JPY, RMB), rupees (₹), CHF and prefixed dollars (A$, C$; the letter before '$' makes FIGURE_RE skip the symbol) carry no currency, so '$5 billion' matches '¥5 billion' or '5 billion yen', and '$50M' matches 'A$50M'. (c) Year binding is skipped when the claim's year sits in a comma-separated opener: 'In 2019,' and 'By 2019,' form a segment with no content words, so the year matches any 2019 in the quote ('In 2019, Acme was founded ...' against '... founded ... in 2015 and acquired ... in 2019'). That is a re-ordering of the r3 year-swap probe, and the most common way English places a year. (d) A figure with no noun after it matches when either of its two nearest preceding words appears before the quote figure. A shared verb is enough, so 'Acme revenue grew 30%' matches 'Acme revenue grew 10% and Acme margins grew 30%', a percentage moved between metrics.

At 3c517f0 the same TSV fails, but only on the range and 'Not even' rows; the currency, year-opener and %-verb rows pass there too (pre-existing, not fixed by this round). Unit probes bin/score4.py and bin/variants.py at HEAD: 'supported' for '$5 billion' vs '5 billion yen', 'JPY 5 billion', 'RMB 5 billion', 'C$50M', 'CHF 50 million'; 'By 2019, Acme had 300 employees' vs '... 300 employees by 2021 and 100 employees in 2019'; 'Acme revenue grew 30%' vs 'Acme revenue grew 10% and Acme margins grew 30%'; 'Acme has 12 offices' vs 'between five and seven offices'; honest 'Acme has between 5 and 7 offices' vs 'between five and seven offices' 'partial [number mismatch]'. $ vs EUR, euros vs dollars and pounds vs dollars are correctly rejected.
issues.suggested_fix: (a) In _words_to_number, 'and' joins only inside a compound ('two hundred and fifty', 'one thousand and one'), that is after hundred/thousand/million; otherwise end the run, so 'two and five' stays two numbers. (b) Recognise ¥/₹/₩/CHF/JPY/CNY/RMB/INR/AUD/CAD and word forms (yen, yuan, rupees, francs), treat a letter-prefixed '$' (A$, C$, HK$, S$, NZ$) as its own currency and leave only 'US$' as '$'. Or make a claim currency fail when the quote figure has an unrecognised symbol next to it. (c) Give the opener segment the stems of the clause it introduces (merge 'In 2019,' with the following segment), or bind years to the whole clause when their own segment has no content words. (d) Without a noun, require the claim's nearest content word (the metric, e.g. 'revenue') rather than any of the two nearest words, and do not count verbs from the change table (grew/fell/rose/cut) as attachment. Add each pair to the fabrication corpus and the digit/word range pair to the honest corpus, and correct quality-gates.md for anything left out of scope.

issues.problem: The cancel flag is checked before Popen, but a process is registered in _LIVE_PROCS only after Popen returns. If the dispatcher is interrupted while a worker thread is between the check and the registration (fork/exec in progress, slower under load), _terminate_live_workers' snapshot misses that process. It then runs to its own timeout (600 s by default) while ThreadPoolExecutor.__exit__ waits for it. This is one paid session and a 10-minute hang after Ctrl-C. The window is milliseconds in normal conditions.
issues.evidence: REVF-H8a4-probe/bin/race4.py widens the window with a Popen wrapper that sleeps 0.5 s before spawning and sends SIGTERM to the dispatcher at +0.2 s (worker timeout 12 s, fake cursor logging START/TERM): fake log '+0.67s START pid=5537' (after the signal), '+12.69s TERM pid=5537' (its own timeout); dispatcher 'KeyboardInterrupt after 12.5'. Without an injected delay, bin/sigdrive3.py never hits it.
issues.suggested_fix: Close the gap under the lock: after Popen, add the process to _LIVE_PROCS while holding _LIVE_LOCK and re-check _CANCEL there (kill the group and raise KeyboardInterrupt when it is set). Have the interrupt path set _CANCEL while holding the same lock, before it snapshots the processes.

issues.problem: The short-sentence rule says a sentence of 30 characters or fewer is a claim when it names a thing. But _has_name counts any capitalised first word that is not on the starter list as a name. So almost every short sentence of three or more words becomes a factual claim, and if uncited it fails --strict: transitions and evaluations such as 'Next, we compare costs.', 'Pricing is simple.', 'Documentation is thin.' and 'Setup took minutes.'. All of these were excluded at 3c517f0. Long sentences of the same kind were already claims, so this is mostly a consistency change, but it contradicts the documentation. 'Next, we compare costs.' is navigation, the class the round meant to exclude.
issues.evidence: bin probe (inline): extract_claims._long_enough at HEAD -> True for 'Pricing is simple.', 'Support is responsive.', 'Setup took minutes.', 'Next, we compare costs.', 'Documentation is thin.' (all classified factual); at 3c517f0 -> False. 'We compared 4 vendors.' and 'See Figure 3 below.' are now correctly excluded, and the r3 short fabrications ('Acme is HIPAA compliant.', 'Acme never had a breach.', 'Microsoft owns Acme outright.') are now extracted (re-run of r3 runs/short: 6 claims, the 3 fabrications unsupported, strict fail).
issues.suggested_fix: Count the opener as a name only when it is an acronym, camelCase, an identifier, or followed by another capitalised word, and add transition openers ('next', 'below', 'above', 'first', 'finally') to NAVIGATION_RE. Or document that every short sentence of three or more words is a claim.
